note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following rising PSA and PI-RADS 5 lesion despite initial ISUP grade group 1 biopsy.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer follow-up. Recently retired shopkeeper, married, living with partner. Medical history includes type 2 diabetes managed with empagliflozin, COPD on tiotropium and salbutamol PRN, and osteoarthritis. Patient cycles five times weekly for commuting and consumes approximately seven units of alcohol weekly. Reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms (IPSS 14). No recent bone pain or haematuria. Recent colonoscopy surveillance was unremarkable. Flexible appointment scheduling requested due to self-employed status.

Per rectum, a firm nodule is palpable in the right lateral aspect of the prostate, consistent with clinical T2a staging. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.

admin: Patient self-employed; flexible appointment slots requested.
